subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by a shared core session-lock/self-heal fix, or by explicit retry/coalescing in the affected inbound surfaces?
rationale: Automation should not choose this owner boundary: per-channel retry matches Telegram precedent, while the latest source comment argues that a root session-lock fix avoids repeatedly porting the same recovery across channels.

options.title: Choose Shared Core Fix
options.body: Use the reply-session initialization owner boundary to serialize or self-heal the conflict once across WebChat, heartbeat, Slack, Signal, Discord, and future channels.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Add explicit retry or coalescing to each inbound path that can currently terminalize the conflict, even if shared recovery is later improved.

options.title: Ask For Current-Main Live Proof
options.body: Request a WebChat or heartbeat reproduction on current main before selecting the permanent fix layer.

recommendation.title: Choose Shared Core Fix
recommendation.body: Use the reply-session initialization owner boundary to serialize or self-heal the conflict once across WebChat, heartbeat, Slack, Signal, Discord, and future channels.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where jalehman has the strongest recent history.
